title: Production Lead Engine
audience: Advanced developers and agencies whose prospecting automation has become important enough that hidden workflow state, fragile recovery, and unclear concurrency are now business risks.
shortDescription: Move mission-critical prospecting state into a real software system with PostgreSQL, durable jobs, workers, provider boundaries, testing, observability, and recovery you can reason about.
coreOutcome: Replace workflow sprawl with an application architecture you can inspect, test, recover, and extend when the lead engine has become too important to live inside execution history.
problem: The automation now carries enough campaigns, state, failures, and money that workflow convenience is starting to cost control.
hook: When the automation becomes mission-critical, workflow history is not enough.
reframe:
n8n is useful when a workflow is the right unit of execution. The problem begins when the workflow quietly becomes the system of record for several campaigns, retries, suppression, recovery, concurrency, and business history. At that point, a convenient automation can become difficult to reason about precisely when you most need to trust it.

Production requirements feel unnecessary until a failure leaves you asking basic questions you cannot answer cleanly. Which lead state is authoritative? Which job is safe to retry? Did two workers touch the same record? Can you reconstruct why this email was sent? Can a provider failure recover without replaying the wrong work?

Production Lead Engine moves those responsibilities into software built to own them. PostgreSQL becomes the source of truth. Durable jobs define bounded work. Workers run under explicit retry, deduplication, and concurrency policies. Provider adapters isolate external services. Tests protect behavior you already proved in earlier tiers. Observability makes state changes inspectable. This is not infrastructure theater. It is what you build when losing control has become more expensive than adding architecture.

delivery.length: Advanced implementation guide for a database-backed prospecting application using TypeScript, PostgreSQL, durable jobs, workers, and production controls.
delivery.worksheets: Domain model, schema map, job policies, provider contracts, concurrency rules, retry and dedupe strategy, observability checklist, and deployment plan.
delivery.time: Build only after a lower-tier campaign has proven both the commercial process and the need for application-level control.

proof.title: The campaign can be inspected without asking a workflow what happened.
proof.body: A lead, finding, activity, suppression event, campaign, and job exists as durable state independent of the worker currently processing it. Recovery and audit stop depending on reconstructing business history from execution logs.
proof.before: Workflow execution history is carrying business state, retries, and recovery logic across several campaigns.
proof.after: PostgreSQL owns durable state, the queue owns job policy, and workers execute bounded responsibilities against explicit records.

situation: A proven automated pipeline now matters enough that durable recovery, auditability, concurrency, and testing are no longer optional technical niceties.
commonFailure: Stretching workflow execution into application state hides ownership, recovery, testing, and concurrency until the system is hardest to change.
methodology: Model prospecting around PostgreSQL records, durable queue jobs, bounded workers, provider adapters, webhooks, observability, tests, and explicit operational policies.
capabilities: Own campaign and lead state outside workflow execution history
Recover durable jobs under explicit retry, deduplication, and concurrency policies
Test, deploy, observe, and operate a lead engine that has become important business infrastructure
contents: When a workflow should become an application
PostgreSQL domain model for campaigns, leads, findings, activity, suppression, and jobs
Durable job queue design, retries, deduplication, concurrency, and recovery
Worker boundaries and provider adapters for evidence, AI, enrichment, and email services
Webhook handling for replies, delivery events, bounces, and suppression
Application-level campaign limits, stop states, and safety controls
Testing strategy for state transitions, workers, providers, and failure cases
Observability, deployment, maintenance, and production operations
whoItsFor: Advanced developers and agencies with prospecting automation important enough to justify production controls
Teams managing multiple campaigns or meaningful concurrency
Builders who are more worried about recovery and auditability than keeping the architecture simple
whoItsNotFor: Anyone whose needs are still met by supervised ChatGPT workflows or n8n
Anyone who has not validated the underlying prospecting process
Beginners looking for the fastest way to automate a small campaign

faqs.question: Why not keep extending n8n?
faqs.answer: You can until the operational cost of hidden state, recovery, concurrency, testing, and auditability becomes greater than the convenience of staying workflow-centered. This tier is for that point, not before it.

faqs.question: What is the system of record?
faqs.answer: PostgreSQL. Workers and services act on durable records rather than treating workflow execution history as business state.

faqs.question: Is this a starter product?
faqs.answer: No. If the architecture sounds like more burden than relief, use a lower tier. This product assumes advanced development ability and a prospecting process already proven at lower levels.

faqs.question: Does this cover deployment and operations?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scope includes testing, observability, deployment, recovery, maintenance, and production controls because the point is an operable system, not a code sample.

stateModel: PostgreSQL is the system of record; a queue job is the unit of execution
supervision: Production monitoring, maintenance, and exception operations
technicalBoundary: Workers and services orchestrate bounded responsibilities. Database and queue policies own durable state, retries, and deduplication.
